How to play

  1. Pick a size, then drag in space to throw it. Longer drag = faster.
  2. The dotted line shows where it will go. Let go to throw.
  3. Too slow and it falls in. Too fast and it escapes. Just right and it orbits.

What's happening?

  • Everything pulls on everything else. Heavier pulls harder. Twice as far away pulls 4 times weaker. That's Newton's law of gravity.
  • An orbit is falling and missing: the planet falls towards the star, but it's going sideways so fast it keeps missing.
  • When two bodies crash they merge. The new body keeps their total momentum (mass × velocity), so the momentum number doesn't change.
  • The energy number stays almost fixed too. A crash turns some into heat, so it drops a little then.
  • The Figure-8 is a real solution found in 2000: three equal stars chasing each other along one loop. Nudge it and it falls apart.

Try this: on Sun + planets, throw a moon so it swings close past a planet and gets flung away much faster. That's a slingshot, the trick space probes use to reach the outer planets.
